rows.gloss: not because of difference of domain
if sometimes equality of domain then subordination and overriding
rows.morph: compound: kvacit+sometimes, viṣaya+domain, tulyatva+equality, bādhya+subordinated, bādhakatā+overriding

items.question: When can Vedic scripture override the word of Shiva?
premises: Vedic scripture does not override the word of Shiva merely because their domains differ.
A relation of subordination and overriding arises only when their domains are equal.
Such equality of domain may occur in some cases.
items.inference: Therefore, Vedic scripture can override the word of Shiva only in cases where both apply to the same domain.
uncertainties: The exact scope of viṣaya-tulyatva in this ritual-epistemic context is not fully specified in this verse.
items.plain_english: Thus, Vedic scripture does not override the word of Shiva simply because their domains differ. If, in some case, their domains are the same, then a relation of being overridden and overriding can arise.

rows.grounds: status of Vedic scripture in that case
ritual installation on body and vessels

rows.gloss: on the body and the offering vessel

items.question: What does the text do after settling the scriptural conflict?
premises: When domains are equal, Vedic scripture is the one overridden.
This point has already been explained earlier.
The exposition now returns to the main ritual topic.
items.inference: Having settled the authority issue, the text resumes the ritual procedure by prescribing placement on the body and the offering vessel.
uncertainties: The specific type of nyāsa intended here is not named in this verse.
items.plain_english: In that case, it is Vedic scripture that is overridden; this has already been explained before. Now we return to the matter at hand: having made the placement on the body and on the offering vessel, we continue.

rows.gloss: with drops of water from the common offering vessel
rows.morph: compound: sāmānya+common, argha+offering, pātra+vessel, ambhas+water, vipruḍ+drops; f.ins.pl

items.question: What ritual steps follow the placement on the body and offering vessel?
premises: The practitioner uses drops of water from the common offering vessel.
All worship equipment is sprinkled for purification.
The external worship is performed after this purification.
items.inference: After the placement, one should sprinkle all worship equipment with water from the common offering vessel and then perform the external worship.
items.plain_english: Having sprinkled all the worship equipment with drops of water from the common offering vessel, one should then perform the external worship.
